tagline: Match the correct number to each stat

questions.question: How many grass courts host official matches
questions.more: Exactly eighteen show courts, including Centre Court, host the official tournament matches.

questions.question: What height in mm is the grass mown daily
questions.more: Groundskeepers maintain the grass at exactly 8mm for optimum ball bounce and speed.

questions.question: How many matches needed to win the singles title
questions.more: A player must win seven consecutive knockout rounds to lift the trophy.

questions.question: Federer: how many consecutive Wimbledon titles from 2003
questions.more: Federer matched Bjorn Borg's modern record before Rafael Nadal broke his streak in 2008.

questions.question: Wimbledon moved to Church Rd in the year 19??
questions.more: The tournament moved in 1922, which marked the grand opening of the current Centre Court.

questions.question: Length in minutes of the shortest ladies singles final
questions.more: Steffi Graf defeated Natasha Zvereva 6-0, 6-0 in just thirty-four minutes in 1988.

questions.question: How many letters are in the element with the longest name?
questions.more: Rutherfordium — named after physicist Ernest Rutherford — is the longest common element name, honouring a scientist widely considered the father of nuclear physics.

questions.question: How many total horizontal rows make up the modern periodic table?
questions.more: The seven rows represent the number of electron shells an element possesses.

questions.question: What is the atomic number of Neon, the gas used in glowing signs?
questions.more: Neon is an unreactive noble gas that glows reddish-orange when electrified.

questions.question: What is the atomic number of Calcium, the metal required for strong bones?
questions.more: Calcium is an alkaline earth metal and the fifth most abundant element in the human body.

questions.question: How many naturally occurring elements belong to the Halogen family in Group 17?
questions.more: The five natural halogens are Fluorine, Chlorine, Bromine, Iodine, and Astatine.

questions.question: How many elements start with the letter C?
questions.more: Cadmium, Caesium, Calcium, Californium, Carbon, Cerium, Chlorine, Chromium, Cobalt, Copernicium, Copper, and Curium — twelve in total.

tagline: In which sports are these terms used?

questions.question: googly
questions.more: A leg-spinner's delivery that unexpectedly spins inward toward a right-handed batsman instead of outward — the sport is cricket.

questions.question: nutmeg
questions.more: A skillful move where a player kicks, passes, or dribbles the ball directly through an opponent's legs — the sport is soccer.

questions.question: shank
questions.more: A severely mis-hit shot where the ball strikes the club's hosel, causing it to shoot sharply and uncontrollably off-line — the sport is golf.

questions.question: plumber
questions.more: Hockey slang for a gritty, blue-collar player who focuses on physical defensive work and battles along the boards rather than highlight-reel skill — the sport is ice hockey.

questions.question: garryowen
questions.more: A tactical, high up-and-under kick designed to hang in the air, giving the chasing team time to sprint forward and pressure the catcher — the sport is rugby.

questions.question: brick
questions.more: A heavily mis-hit shot that clangs violently off the rim or backboard with no real chance of going in — the sport is basketball.

tagline: Match the right letter to each question and feel your brain hurting

questions.question: First letter of the shortest state name in New England.
questions.more: Maine, at just five letters, is the shortest of the six New England state names.

questions.question: Last letter of the last state name alphabetically.
questions.more: Wyoming is the final state alphabetically among all fifty, and its name ends in the letter G.

questions.question: Last letter of the state that has a capital of Albany.
questions.more: Albany has been the capital of New York State since 1797 — and 'New York' ends in the letter K.

questions.question: The third letter of the state that the Mississippi river has the longest stretch in.
questions.more: Minnesota contains more miles of the Mississippi River than any other state, thanks to its many bends as the river begins its winding journey south.

questions.question: The second letter of the state that has the highest point.
questions.more: Alaska's Denali, at 20,310 feet, is the highest point of any U.S. state and the highest peak in North America.

questions.question: The first letter of the state name with the lowest ratio of syllables to consonants.
questions.more: Washington packs seven consonants into just three syllables, giving it one of the lowest syllable-to-consonant ratios of any state name.

tagline: Who knew sports were so colourful?

questions.question: What colour cap is worn by the starting goalkeeper of a water polo team?
questions.more: Water polo goalkeepers wear a red cap, distinguishing them from teammates' blue or white caps, since only the keeper may use both hands on the ball inside the defensive area.

questions.question: In snooker, what colour is the ball that must be potted immediately after the yellow ball when clearing the colours?
questions.more: When clearing the colours at the end of a frame, they must be potted in ascending value order: yellow, green, brown, blue, pink, then black.

questions.question: In rugby union, what colour card does the ref show a player to send them to the sin bin?
questions.more: A yellow card sends a rugby union player to the sin bin for 10 minutes, while a red card is a permanent dismissal for the rest of the match.

questions.question: In cycling, what colour jersey is awarded to the overall leader of the Giro d'Italia race?
questions.more: The maglia rosa (pink jersey) has been awarded to the Giro d'Italia's overall leader since 1931, its colour chosen to match the pink pages of La Gazzetta dello Sport, the race's founding newspaper.

questions.question: In curling, what colour is the outermost ring of the target area (the house) on the ice?
questions.more: Curling's house uses a standardised blue outer ring with a white middle ring and red centre, adopted so TV audiences worldwide can judge stone position at a glance.

questions.question: In ice hockey, what is the usual colour of the puck?
questions.more: Ice hockey pucks are made of vulcanised rubber and are traditionally black so they stand out clearly against the white ice.
